claims.claim: Python (Flask/FastAPI): the interpreter and framework typically take 30–60 MB resident
claims.measured: Idle: FastAPI 40 MB, Flask 115 MB (gthread 52 MB, gevent 60 MB). Peak: FastAPI 41–47 MB, Flask 117–123 MB
claims.why: FastAPI and the threaded or gevent Flask variants fall inside 30–60 MB, and even plain Flask at 115 MB is within 2x of the upper bound.

claims.claim: Python (Flask/FastAPI) takes noticeably longer than a second to start on a Cortex-A53
claims.measured: Start-up: FastAPI 895 ms, Flask 996 ms (gthread 606 ms, gevent 841 ms) on a much faster x86 Ultra 9
claims.why: They already take close to a second on a fast x86 core, so taking well over a second on a slower Cortex-A53 is within a factor of 2.

claims.claim: Node.js has a larger baseline memory footprint than Python
claims.measured: Idle: Node 38–43 MB vs Python 40 MB (FastAPI) and 52–115 MB (Flask variants). Plaintext peak: Node 55–57 MB vs FastAPI 41 MB and Flask 55–117 MB
claims.why: At idle Node used about the same memory as FastAPI and less than every Flask variant, so the claim points the wrong way.

claims.claim: Go: a static binary using the standard library's HTTP server would fit in the budget (under 20 MB, start in under 1 s)
claims.measured: Idle 2 MB, peak 7–15 MB across tests, start-up 238 ms
claims.why: Measured memory and start-up are both well inside the 20 MB and 1 s limits.

claims.claim: Full frameworks (Axum, Actix) and async Rust bring an async runtime that inflates memory and runtime size
claims.measured: Idle 1 MB, peak 3–10 MB, image 79–83 MB, start-up 238–239 ms
claims.why: There is no measurement of a synchronous tiny_http server to compare with, though Axum and Actix were already the smallest servers measured, at 1 MB idle.

claims.claim: Choosing C (libmicrohttpd) over Rust costs memory safety in the parser, not the requirements (it would still meet the memory and start-up limits)
claims.why: No C or libmicrohttpd server was measured; the closest is cpp-drogon, which is a different library.
